prerequisites: Knowledge across the breadth of the studied subject

learning_outcomes.text: Students can methodically process practical tasks and present them within a given timeframe with a clearly structured result.

Students have a critical understanding of the most important theories, principles, and methods from their studies, can on this basis familiarize themselves with a new task and independently deepen their knowledge in a special area.
Students can evaluate the state of the literature in the context of the underlying research question and critically reflect on methodical approaches.

Students apply the tools and methods learned and developed during their studies to support their work. On this basis, they develop solution approaches and realize solutions that meet the state of the art.

Students research the state of technology and science and derive innovative approaches for the specific scientific task of their thesis. In their explanations, they present the underlying research results and their innovations.

Students formulate identified technical challenges and solutions, categorize them into an interdisciplinary context, and present them in discourse with experts. They communicate with stakeholders, taking into account their diverse perspectives and interests.

Students develop a professional self-image in the thesis that is oriented towards the goals and standards of professional action in professional fields predominantly outside of science. They recognize situation-appropriately the framework conditions of professional action in relation to the task of their thesis and can reflect their activity in an interdisciplinary context.

syllabus_topics: Recording the state of the art
Developing concepts for solving the task
Developing partial solutions and combining them into an overall concept
Overall consideration and evaluation of the solution
Presenting the solution in the form of the Bachelor thesis
Presenting the results in a colloquium
assessment_rules: Graded examination performance includes the final thesis and colloquium. 12 ECTS are awarded for the Bachelor thesis and 3 ECTS for the colloquium. The Bachelor thesis should be 40-70 pages long. The colloquium duration is 15-45 minutes.
